newsitem.title: USA: Dow index edges to record despite fears of rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Dow index edges to record despite fears of rate hike.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average edged higher to set a record for a second session Tuesday, but the overall market was nervous because of speculation that the Federal Reserve might be planning an interest rate hike.

The Dow closed up 5.77 points at 7,085.16, beating Monday's record finish of 7,079.39. In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,290 to 1,180 on active volume of 491 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

"The market is very divided on the outlook for interest rate policy," said Charles White, managing director at Avatar Associates. "Right now there's no compelling evidence to drive us in either direction."
Investors were worried about Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's warnings recently that stocks could be overvalued and that the central bank might raise short-term interest rates.

In the bond market, the 30-year Treasury bond was off 14/32, or $4.375 per $1,000 face value, which raised its yield to 6.85 percent from Monday's close of 6.82 percent. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
Analysts said the market was likely to become even more cautious ahead of the meeting of the Fed's policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) on March 25.
The latest economic data unnerved some investors.

The Labour Department said labour costs rose 2.5 percent in the fourth quarter after a 1.4 percent increase in the third quarter and productivity rose 1.1 percent after a 2.2 percent rise in the third quarter.
The numbers are closely watched since gains in productivity, which allow businesses to increase their output without raising their costs, are seen as crucial to containing inflation.
"Basically, this market has been put on wait," said Alfred Goldman, technical analyst at A.G. Edwards & Sons. "We're going to have more of this ragged action until we get past the FOMC meeting."
Within the mixed picture of the overall market, there were some subtle shifts at play, analysts noted, with investors taking profits in strong sectors and buying up some recent laggards.
"Some of the groups that have had outstanding performances appeared to be catching their breath," White said, citing banking and pharmaceutical issues in particular.
Among drug stocks, Amgen Inc. lost 1-1/2 to 61-1/4 and Eli Lilly & Co. shed 2-3/4 to 88-3/4.
Chase Manhattan Corp. slipped 3-1/8 to 106-1/2 and BankAmerica Corp. fell 3-3/8 to 119-5/8.

Steel companies finished broadly higher, led by USX-U.S. Steel Corp., which gained 1-3/8 to 30-1/8 and Inland Steel Industries Inc. up 1 to 20-1/8, after an industry report showed shipments from U.S. steel mills rose by 7.3 percent in January vs. a month earlier.
The increase was 5.5 percent when compared to a year ago, according the report by the American Iron and Steel Institute.

Stocks got a vote of confidence from Fidelity Investments' Magellan Fund, which said it increased the percentage of its portfolio invested in stocks to 93.5 percent at the end of January from 89.6 percent in December.

Fidelity said Intel Corp., General Electric Co. and Philip Morris Cos. remained Magellan's top three stock holdings, but that General Motors Corp. was replaced by Citicorp among the fund's top 10 holdings.
Among individual issues, Tessco Technologies Inc. tumbled 12-3/8 to 20-1/8 after the company warned that quarterly earnings would be below analysts' estimates.
Wyle Electronics slid 5 to 33-3/8 after it also warned about upcoming earnings.
Nike Inc. fell 5/8 to 66-3/8, rebounding from a session low of 63 on a rumour that Woolworth Corp.'s Foot Locker unit had reduced orders for Nike athletic shoes. Woolworth later denied the rumour.
The Nasdaq Composite index fell 5.96 points to 1,316.76.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks fell 2.31 to 811.34. The American Stock Exchange index was off 0.20 to 603.43.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks fell 0.64 to 427.06. The average share was down 6 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,741.154 down 15.889 or 0.20 percent.
